title: How Well Do You Know Metric Units?
intro: Eight questions on SI units and conversions. Pick one answer per question; your score and the answers show at the end.

questions.text: How many base units make up the International System of Units (SI)?
questions.explanation: Every other SI unit, such as the newton or the watt, is built from these base units.

source.quote: The SI is made up of 7 base units that define the 22 derived units with special names and symbols

questions.text: SI prefixes scale a unit up or down by powers of which number?
questions.explanation: That is why converting between metric units only moves the decimal point.

source.quote: used to represent smaller or larger units by factors that are powers of 10

questions.text: How many centimeters are in 2.5 meters?
questions.explanation: One meter is 100 centimeters, so 2.5 x 100 = 250.

questions.text: How many grams are in 3 kilograms?
questions.explanation: One kilogram is 1,000 grams, so 3 x 1,000 = 3,000.

questions.text: A recipe needs 750 milliliters of stock. How many liters is that?
Which is longer: 1.2 kilometers or 1,150 meters?
questions.explanation: 1.2 kilometers is 1,200 meters, which is 50 meters more than 1,150.

questions.text: How many millimeters are in 4 centimeters?
questions.explanation: One centimeter is 10 millimeters, so 4 x 10 = 40.

questions.text: A runner covers 5,000 meters. How many kilometers is that?

results.title: Keep Practicing
results.description: A few conversions tripped you up. Write the steps down once (1 kilometer is 1,000 meters, 1 meter is 100 centimeters) and try again.

results.title: Solid Basics
results.description: You know the common units. The misses were mostly decimal places, so check which way the point moves before you answer.

results.title: Metric Pro
results.description: You moved between units without slipping. The prefixes and the powers of 10 behind them are second nature to you.
